newsitem.title: GERMANY: Buba's Sievert-no scope for rate cut at present.
newsitem.headline: Buba's Sievert-no scope for rate cut at present.

text.p: Bundesbank council member Olaf Sievert said there was no scope at present for a cut in German interest rates but it was still open as to how the monetary policy situation would look after a few months.
"I do not want to agree that the interest rate cut cycle of the Bundesbank is over," Sievert said in a magazine interview.
"From today's point of view there is no further scope in the short term. But it is still open how things will look after several months."
Buba's Sievert-no scope for rate cut at present
The interview with German Boerse Online magazine was made available ahead of publication on Thursday.

Sievert, who is also president of the state central bank of Saxony and Thuringia, said there was still potential for a fall in bond yields and that the current economic upturn in Germany gave no cause to fear a resurgence of inflation.
Even with a strong economic recovery, bond yields need not inevitably rise, Sievert said.
